---
title: "Failures log"
---

Everything that was tried and did not work, false alarms included. Test twenty signals and one
will look significant by chance, so the count of attempts is part of every result.

## Signals and models tried

| Date | Module | What was tried | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-14 | Tech Value | First live evaluation: cores-times-clock baseline, plain regression and AutoGluon on 13,388 SPEC results. | Validation picked the AutoGluon ensemble. On the holdout it beat the baseline (0.222 against 0.488 mean absolute log error, fold spread 0.143), so the test passes. The plain regression, which validation did not pick, scored 0.102 on the same holdout. The pick was not changed after seeing this: choosing by holdout score would turn the holdout into a tuning set. |
| 2026-11-14 | Tech Value | Price sources: Best Buy API, eBay Browse API, and a crawler probe of 24 US retailers. | Best Buy issues keys to company emails only. eBay's licence forbids stored price history and price statistics. 17 retailers block automated clients and 4 disallow search pages in robots.txt. One retailer (Central Computers) is crawled, so the value ranking covers a small part of the market. |
| 2026-11-15 | Macro Monitor | Forecast test: ten AutoGluon TimeSeries models on the monthly moves of 51 series, against four rules of thumb. Fitted before November 2023, picked on the next twelve months, scored once on 1,176 one-month-ahead forecasts from November 2024 to October 2026. | No signal found. Validation picked AutoGluon's weighted ensemble; on the holdout its scaled error was 0.638 against 0.658 for the best rule of thumb (the series' average move), an improvement of 0.020 against a fold spread of 0.052. The baseline is published and no forecast appears on the site. |
| 2026-11-15 | Macro Monitor | Flag rule (2.5 spreads against ten years of own history, and against neighbours), backtested over the 24 months to October 2026. | 61 own-history flags in 1,177 readings, 5.2% against the 1.2% a bell curve would give, so most flags reflect fat tails, not rare events. Of the 52 old enough to judge, 42 held and 10 reversed. Of 18 neighbour flags, 14 held and 3 reversed. The threshold was not changed after seeing this. |
| 2026-11-15 | Macro Monitor | Catalogue grows to 70 series: 19 IMF series added, 4 BIS series that the BIS does not publish removed. | Rules unchanged. The flag backtest and the forecast test are re-scored on the next weekly run on the larger set. That is a different population, so its counts get their own row here and the two rows above stay as they are. |
| 2026-11-15 | Energy Demand | Oil product demand from JODI-Oil as a second measure beside electricity (it has all seven economies, Indonesia included). | Not built. JODI's terms of use reserve all rights in the site and grant no right to reuse the data. Electricity demand from Ember (CC BY 4.0) is the only measure, which leaves Indonesia out. |
| 2026-11-15 | Trade and Supply Chain | Lead-time test: does the growth of US imports from an economy improve a same-month estimate of that economy's total export growth over last month's growth? A straight line fitted to December 2022, scored once on January 2023 to mid-2026 (42 or 43 months), for six economies. Rules written before any trade figure was collected. | No signal found for any of the six. The bar was a gain of more than twice its standard error. Vietnam came closest: error 6.68 against 8.88 for the baseline, a gain of 2.20 with a standard error of 1.13 (1.9 times). Malaysia 0.54 (standard error 0.30), the Philippines 0.57 (0.74), Singapore 0.21 (0.47), Thailand 0.05 (0.66), Indonesia -0.25 (1.02). The claim is dropped and the bar was not moved for Vietnam. Six economies were tested, so one near-pass is about what chance gives. |
| 2026-11-16 | Demand Radar | Four tests, fixed before any figure was fetched: does last month's change on a year earlier in English Wikipedia pageviews (a fixed list of articles per category) improve a forecast of this month's change in US retail sales (Census MARTS, not seasonally adjusted) over last month's change in sales? Fitted to December 2021, scored once on January 2022 to September 2026. Pass at a gain of more than twice its standard error. | No signal found in any pair. Electronics and appliances -0.35 points (bar 0.95), furniture -0.09 (0.69), clothing -5.06 (1.21), sporting goods, hobby, music and books +0.04 (0.49). The radar does not become a module. |
| 2026-11-15 | Federal Procurement | Exit criterion: for every month from October 2016, federal obligations for computer hardware summed from USAspending's transaction download must be within 1% of the monthly figure from USAspending's own search with the same filters. Written before the figures were computed, after a test of one fiscal year had already shown gaps. | Not met. 95 of 121 months are within 1%; 26 are not, the worst (January 2026) by 14.2%. Over the whole period the search figure is 0.8% higher. The limit was not moved and no month was dropped. The pages use the download and show this verdict. (A first diagnosis that grouped the search's rows by internal id was wrong: that id belongs to the award, so separate modifications share it. It is replaced by the row-by-row check below.) |
| 2026-11-15 | Federal Procurement | Second check, added after the criterion above failed and after 8 months had been compared: in every month outside the limit, match the search's transactions to the download's one by one on award, modification, date and amount. A month reconciles if no listed transaction is missing from the download and, with exact second copies removed, the two figures agree within 0.1%. A new test; the first verdict stands. | 25 of 26 months reconcile; one (October 2024) could not be listed because USAspending dropped the connection, and is retried weekly. In all 25, every one of the 65,042 transactions the search lists is in the download. The search lists 288 transactions a second time, worth $442.6 million; with those removed the worst gap is 0.0004%. The difference is double counting in USAspending's search figure, not missing data in the download. |

## Collector repairs

A source that needs more than two repairs in a month is downgraded to a manual monthly entry,
or dropped.

| Date | Source | What broke | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-14 | SPEC CPU 2017 | First live run stopped: the schema rejected a result with a 2007 hardware-availability date. | The lower bound was too tight (2010). SPEC CPU 2017 has been run on older hardware; bound moved to 2000. |
| 2026-11-14 | Tech Value | A second and third price source. Zones and PCNation were checked in detail, then 30 more US stores were probed. | Zones builds its result list in the browser and PCNation disallows search in robots.txt. Of the 30 others, 5 answered a polite crawler and all 5 list mostly whole computers, not parts. In total 54 stores were tested and one is usable, so every price still comes from a single store. The first live crawl also kept 24 whole computers as part listings, and two set the price of a processor until the filter was fixed. |
| 2026-11-14 | Tech Value | A fair price model: predict a part's price from its Blender score with a straight line, a line with brand, and a random forest, against a naive baseline of one price per point of score. | With 20 graphics cards and 25 processors that have two or more listings, no model beat the baseline by more than twice the standard error of its gain. The baseline sets the fair price, which makes the gap a restatement of score per dollar. The models stay on the leaderboard and are re-tested on every run. |
| 2026-11-15 | IMF | Before storing anything, the unit check stopped Singapore's trade twice: exports jump 3.1 times in January 2004 and imports 2.9 times in January 2010. | Both are breaks in the source's basis, not real moves. Every IMF series now starts in January 2011. |
| 2026-11-15 | Blender Open Data | The first live slice showed what the parser filed as "unreadable" (about 14% of launches): Blender 2.x launches in the newer file layout, which report render time instead of samples per minute. | Filed as `old_schema`, a different measurement, and kept out of the scores as before. The next weekly run's counts will show whether that is all of the 14%. |
| 2026-11-15 | Schedule | The daily run due 09:17 UTC had not started by 10:20 UTC; the day before, the run due at the same time started at about 15:52 UTC. | GitHub starts scheduled runs late on free accounts. The heartbeat allows 48 hours, so a delay of hours is not an alarm; a missing day is. |
| 2026-11-16 | Retail crawler (fire drill) | Made to fail on purpose: the daily run was started on main with `fire_drill` on, to test the failure path. | Worked as designed: every later step and the site job were skipped, nothing was committed, the site kept the 15 November deploy, and Issue #24 opened 22 seconds after the start. Closed with a note. |
| 2026-11-15 | Schedule | On the next day, no scheduled daily run had appeared by 16:20 UTC, seven hours after 09:17. | Started by hand at 16:25; the late scheduled run then arrived at 16:26 and both succeeded. A second daily slot at 19:47 UTC now runs the pipeline only when no run has succeeded that day. |
